title: Harvard Data Selection: thematic section map and explicit gaps
scope: Every pinned source line has a disposition. Mapping and byte-level tests are not proof of pedagogical completeness. All three recorded reader gaps have scoped explanation, source, execution and visual reviews. Existing audits retain their recorded limitations; this is not a whole-course or English-textbook completion claim.

source_findings.proxy: EL2N/GraNd/entropy/information gain are not the same measured quantity; high error can indicate a wrong label, minority case or model weakness.
source_findings.geometry: The k-center guarantee is geometric under stated assumptions, not an accuracy guarantee. Source language 'facility-location-style' does not introduce another algorithm.
source_findings.dedup: Lexical Jaccard is not generic paraphrase equivalence; LSH candidate recall/complexity and thresholds need actual corpus assumptions. Hash equality needs the declared canonicalization and collision handling.
source_findings.synthetic: Unconditional domain marginals do not determine labels; sample count does not establish independent parents, correct labels, privacy or an optimal synthetic ratio.
source_findings.systems: Retained fraction, training step count, elapsed time, GPU-hours, I/O and money need separate boundaries. Gains across unchanged and changed stages do not universally multiply.
source_findings.measurement: Assigned scenarios, synthetic curves and forecasts are not observed benchmarks or universal thresholds. PPD/AULC/DCR need units and fixed evaluation boundaries.
source_findings.licensing: Pinned QMD uses CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. The separately archived web-edition figures use CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 and remain complete, unmodified objects.

sections.heading: Purpose and metadata
sections.notes: The introductory goals are developed through corpus provenance and end-to-end selection costs; no new introduction copied.

sections.heading: Fundamentals and human-data projection
sections.notes: Corpus availability, reuse and evaluation are covered. The extrapolation is link-only, not a verified exhaustion date; it is not needed as a prerequisite for selection.

sections.heading: Definition of selection
sections.notes: Separate candidate pool, score, selected IDs, schedule and quality constraint. Fewer retained records alone do not prove fewer training operations.

sections.heading: Systems perspective
sections.notes: Account for preparation, training, bytes, annotation, elapsed time and recurring work separately.

sections.heading: Information-compute ratio and triad
sections.notes: The ICR clarification distinguishes conceptual information gain from measured proxies and PPD units. The triad is omitted for recorded explanatory inconsistency, not claimed visually rendered.

sections.heading: ICR frontier and proxy selection setup
sections.notes: EL2N/GraNd/forgetting have definitions, executable source-faithful examples and validation boundaries. High score is not proof of usefulness or boundary proximity.

sections.heading: Static pruning and smaller datasets
sections.notes: Compare full and random equal-size controls, stable record IDs, retained fractions, quality and update budgets. Source compute savings are conditional on fixed epochs.

sections.heading: Coreset algorithms and EL2N workflow
sections.notes: k-center and herding are separately derived and executed; proxy-based scoring remains distinct. The uncertainty-sampling sketch is not passed off as a general geometric coreset. No separate facility-location algorithm is derived in this source range.

sections.heading: Deduplication, images and DLRM cold IDs
sections.notes: Exact/MinHash/LSH remain in the text-corpus chapter. Its image section now develops byte/pixel matching, perceptual hashes, embedding similarity, candidate verification and false removals. The DLRM section develops cold-ID cutoff, remapping, allocation, optimizer state, managed ownership and held-out tail evaluation. Source percentages are explicitly not imported; scoped acceptance is in 2026-10-29-selection-gaps.md.

sections.heading: Quality pruning and dynamic-selection introduction
sections.notes: Confident Learning now develops the label-error gap with OOF probabilities, class thresholds, literal/estimated counts, executable examples, candidate review and rare-class/model-error counterexamples. The source's broad assertion that confident disagreements are usually annotation mistakes is not generalized; label issues are distinguished from confirmed errors.

sections.heading: Curriculum learning
sections.notes: Existing chapter 53 develops curriculum ordering and experimental budgets. A pacing change does not establish lower work at a fixed update count.

sections.heading: Active learning
sections.notes: Pool, acquisition, annotation, refit and held-out evaluation are developed with executed examples and original workflow figures. The hypothetical fourfold curve is not empirical evidence.

sections.heading: Semi-supervised learning
sections.notes: Pseudo-label origin, confidence errors, weak/strong views, masked full-batch denominator, actual small update, graph propagation and label/training-cost distinctions are retained.

sections.heading: Self-supervised learning and amortization
sections.notes: Contrastive and masked reconstruction objectives have separate full readers. The unchanged original amortization figure and actual 10/11-task calculation include upfront pretraining.

sections.heading: Foundation-model reuse
sections.notes: Task-specific adaptation and upfront pretraining are separated; downstream quality is measured, not inferred from pretext loss or a low adaptation cost.

sections.heading: Data augmentation
sections.notes: Label/box/mask transformations, source Mixup/CutMix, policy selection, text/speech constraints and TTA are developed. Back-translation is not reduced to a round trip.

sections.heading: Generative synthesis and domain-gap illustration
sections.notes: GAN/DCGAN and LLM generation have full thematic destinations. A sketch of unconditional marginals cannot determine target decision boundaries; the misleading source use is not adopted.

sections.heading: Sim-to-real, keyword spotting and collapse
sections.notes: Renderer annotations, domain randomization, weighting, GRL/DANN, marginal counterexamples and real-mixture validation are covered. Derived examples are not independent parents/speakers; no universal synthetic mixing ratio or privacy guarantee is adopted.

sections.heading: Knowledge distillation
sections.notes: Existing readers derive temperature/class versus sequence targets, KL directions and student rollouts. Higher teacher entropy does not alone establish useful supervision; accepted bodies are not repeated.

sections.heading: Decision framework
sections.notes: Retain the original English prerequisite table, original Figure 12 and quality-constrained worked choice before cost minimization. Resource constraints can apply simultaneously.

sections.heading: Selection engineering and inequality
sections.notes: Opening 100 versus 5+40 versus 60+40 example includes all preparation. Refresh costs and fixed-epoch/update comparisons are executed. Ten-percent overhead is not a universal break-even rule.

sections.heading: Random-access I/O
sections.notes: Worked IOPS/bytes versus sequential reading, selected shards and bounded shuffle are developed; hardware rates are assigned, not measured specifications.

sections.heading: Data echoing
sections.notes: Fresh visits, downstream presentations, echo placement, steady-state timing and equal-budget comparisons are executed. The primary 3.25 speedup is tied to its actual experiment, not generalized.

sections.heading: Costs, ROI and break-even
sections.notes: Acquisition/annotation/storage/processing, sunk labels, repeated costs and ROI denominators are distinct. Equal-quality claims are not inferred from arithmetic.

sections.heading: Amortization across runs
sections.notes: The first profitable integer run/task is distinguished from equality. Corpus refresh can recur; existing excerpts and calculations are preserved.

sections.heading: Distributed selection and consistency
sections.notes: Local quota counterexample, exact scalar top-k proof, stable score identity, bytes, freshness, cross-shard duplicates and 67-minute scenario are developed. The proof is not generalized to relational coreset objectives.

sections.heading: Cross-layer interactions and optimization stack
sections.notes: The original complete stack is retained with arrow direction and artifact semantics. The 20+80/4=40 example separates fixed work; training-data reduction does not shrink model weights or per-request inference work.

sections.heading: PPD, AULC and DCR
sections.notes: Definitions, units, initial state, trapezoid intermediates, first observed quality budget and executed calculations are retained; storage ratio is not quality-constrained DCR.

sections.heading: Compute frontier, Chinchilla and plotted learning curves
sections.notes: The illustrative PPD plot is retained; the synthetic compute-frontier plot is link-only. Twenty tokens per parameter and a point below a frontier do not uniquely diagnose data starvation.

sections.heading: Fallacies and pitfalls
sections.notes: Existing worked counterexamples cover difficult versus noisy records, distribution/label assumptions, pseudo-label confirmation, omitted selection cost, quality/coverage and synthetic-domain/privacy failure.

sections.heading: Source summary
sections.notes: Covered by the thematic destinations and recorded findings; no duplicate reader recap added.

cold-embedding-ids.required: Show interaction deduplication versus removing/remapping ID rows, table/optimizer memory and lookup effects, OOV policy and held-out recommendation quality. Do not import the source's unsupported 20% interaction -> 30-40% table-memory claim.
cold-embedding-ids.resolution: Retry semantics, frequency policy, OOV remapping, weights and optimizer state, allocation versus traffic, managed slot ownership and unchanged chronological tail evaluation.
